title: Physics of the flying fish: glide data and Thompson's flight envelope
headline: No accessible source gives body mass, fin area and a measured airspeed for the same flying fish (27-row glide table, 7 fetched sources, 2 species first-hand). On what exists the fish is inside Thompson's envelope: v_min 9.85 m/s from its own measured wing loading and lift coefficient, quoted glides 10-20 m/s. NEW: a browser simulator (sim/) of swim, taxi, take-off and glide with every parameter sourced or labelled assumed, pre-registered before its first run; after six logged post-hoc runs it reproduces taxi to 16.5 m/s, 36 m glides of 3 s to 3 m, 288 m in 23 s; the Lean pure-glide bound (35 m) shows why long flights need repeated taxis. Test 4 (the real fish cannot power-fly) is untouched and waits for the physiology chain. NEW part C, labelled HYPOTHETICAL everywhere: a design study of a truly flying 60 g fish from bat, insect and pterosaur values only (no bird): bat-like wing loading of 12 N/m2 needs 3.9x the lifting area (66 cm span), and a 1 m/s climb needs 16 percent flight muscle at the bat-derived maximum specific power (bats average 9 percent, which does not even cover level flight here) and about 930 ml O2 per minute per kg, which only the physiology chain and the Lean O2-to-power bound can rule on. It runs in the same simulator as a second fish and climbs to 42 m in 40 s with the real fish's equations, power-limited only: the O2 supply is not yet applied, and since gills do not ventilate in air the design needs an air-breathing surface (passed to Genotype). Environment locked to conditions/baseline.json. Also new: FishBase length-weight rows for 19 species (18 of 25 rows flagged as unverified estimates), take-off table, Park and Choi's measured ground effect, bridge figure to Daane 2021 fin ratios. R2-R8 proved by Lean; R9 bending written. Birds excluded throughout.
